failure.summary: A phase-local timer can be mistaken for total first-use latency even when it starts after expensive work has already begun and omits deferred GPU work, useful-paint readiness and interaction blocking.

observedSubject.disclosure: R03 correctly states that compileMs starts after nine program submissions and is not total shader compilation or all-material seconds-open evidence.

falsifiableHypothesis: An exact-run, gap-checked phase ledger with injected-delay positive controls and long-task observation will preserve R03 scheduling/visual evidence while refusing an end-to-end or speedup claim when the clock omits pre-wait shader work, first-use GPU delay, useful paint, responsiveness, a controlled pair, or a frozen latency budget.
mustNeverRepeat: rename waitPrograms duration as total shader compilation time
infer a speedup percentage from unmatched environments or cache states
treat non-blocking completion polling as proof that total GPU work decreased
treat phase labels in the UI as proof that the critical path is fully covered
claim responsive interruption without a bound input or long-task observation
promote scheduling correctness or pixel equivalence into seconds-open or user acceptance
applicability: One Fabric Mother trial for first-use or material-switch latency claims. It does not invalidate R03 queue coalescing, stale-result rejection, differential restore, exact artifact identity, visual equivalence, or public runtime evidence.
rollbackPoint: Remove this Candidate if the next exact R02/R03 paired replay shows that existing receipts already provide complete, positive-control-verified end-to-end phase coverage with no added discrimination.
